item_title: Fermenting common ground: a multi-stakeholder brief on fermentation technologies for food and feed
scope_note: Food fermentation in scope; feed parts (feed additives, microbial feed) are context only
vietnam_angle: Vietnam faces the same open question the forum names: whether a product made with a GM microorganism in contained use, with no viable cells or recombinant DNA left, is a GMO product. PO-016 and DMV-16 already ask MAE and MOH to answer it; leading Vietnamese buyers market non-GMO
vietnam_evidence: Decree 43/2026 separates organisms from products and the GMO label applies only above 5% of ingredients (ch07; ch27 option 2); buyers sell non-GMO (ch14). The EU forum, with BEUC, Greenpeace, EEB and industry, also asks to clarify contained-use products, residual GM material (including antibiotic-resistance markers) and harmonised GM labels
verdict_note: Adds to PO-016 a concrete evidence list for 'no viable GMO or recombinant DNA': absence of viable production cells, of recombinant DNA and of antibiotic-resistance markers. Also supports T4 and RM-10 siting: the forum asks for co-owned regional fermentation plants near agricultural hubs. No new candidate
signal_to_watch: EU Biotech Act II definitions for products of GM microorganisms; the European Commission fermentation study; any MAE or MOH written answer to PO-016

item_title: Building a healthy, sustainable, and just EU food system: EU Policy Action Brief guided by EAT-Lancet science
owner: The Protein Project with EAT and partners
scope_note: Diet-change policy: protein split targets, dietary guidelines and consumption shifts. The study does not tell people what to eat and sizes demand only as labelled scenarios
vietnam_angle: None beyond what Part III holds. Public procurement is the one transferable lever and is already covered by the canteen trial and school guidance moves
vietnam_evidence: Vietnam's school guidance (Decision 3958/QD-BYT) already sets no animal share (DMV-17)
verdict_note: Diet-change and consumption-target advocacy (CLAUDE.md scope rules; ch25 section 25.4 on funder fit). Procurement elements already covered by DMV-05 and DMV-17

item_title: From dependency to diversity: a strategic scenario analysis on reducing Europe's soy import dependency by 2035
scope_note: Method in scope; its feed and diet-change levers are context or out of scope for Vietnam
maps_to: RM-01; RM-13; ch22 sections 22.2 and 22.5; app-f4; PSB-009; OQ-462
vietnam_angle: Vietnam imports 98.4% of its soybeans and about 99% of the soy protein it feeds. The study already has the same data foundation (FAO food balance sheets, protein by origin and use) and a forward balance model; what transfers is the target-first back-calculation with feasibility grading and a domestic-feed-only stress test
vietnam_evidence: Run on the study's own numbers (our calculation, tools/vn_backcalc.py): imported soy protein 3.50 Mt in 2025 (feed 3.31, food 0.19); a 20% cut below 2025 by 2035 needs 1.74 Mt of protein (3.8 Mt soybean-meal equivalent) against the S-BASE trend, because trend demand grows 30%. In-scope levers deliver about 9% to 11% of that (domestic soybean at the 2010 area 7.6% to 9.7%, or 14.6% at the 300 kha proposal; D-STRETCH food routes 1.1%); feed efficiency (S-EFF, outside scope) 36.6%; S-ALT 12.1%
verdict_note: The method runs for Vietnam with data the study already holds, except the side-stream and farm-economics levers. It confirms ch22: imports cannot be held near the 2025 level by in-scope levers, and the one in-scope lever with weight for the protein people eat directly is domestic food soybean. Present a feasibility-graded table in app-f4; no change to RM-01 beyond that
signal_to_watch: EU Comprehensive Protein Plan follow-up and the EU harmonised protein balance sheet (VIS-15); China's soy import reduction objective

item_title: Towards a Legume Renaissance in Europe: a practical roadmap for fava beans for food and feed
scope_note: Food legumes in scope; the feed half is context only
maps_to: T10; T1; P6; OQ-463; OQ-094; PSB-006; PSB-010; ch22 section 22.3
vietnam_angle: The roadmap method (one crop, a value-chain taskforce with buyers, a barrier map, a farm-archetype economics model, then policy asks tied to named instruments) fits Vietnam's food soybean, not its feed soybean. Soy foods carry about 181,000 t of protein a year on 97.5% imported beans; domestic non-GM beans have a named buyer with a breeding programme
vietnam_evidence: Food soybean use 540 kt (2025); domestic output 42 to 43 kt; area 205 kha in 2010; domestic beans 25,000 to 30,000 VND/kg against 13,000 to 15,000 for imports (2024), or 1.4 to 1.7 times the 2023 Canadian import unit value of USD 686/t (our calculation); Vinasoy's VSAC holds 2,072 soybean lines and VINASOY 05 yields above 2.5 t/ha at Cu Jut, and QNS plans to invest in soybean raw-material areas in 2026; 654 kha of rice land planned for release by 2030; crop strategy has no soybean target; we found no Vietnamese farm-economics study of soybean or mung bean in rotations
verdict_note: PPE-C1: domestic food-grade soybean (and mung bean) for soy foods and plant drinks, with a buyer-led value-chain taskforce and a farm-economics test as step one. Beats T1 and T10 on public value (domestic inputs for protein people already eat); weak on Vietnam advantage (cost) and defensibility
signal_to_watch: Tonnage of domestic beans bought by Vinasoy and tofu makers (OQ-463); farm-gate soybean price against imported non-GM beans; whether MAE names soybean in its domestic raw-material area task
source_ids: PPE-05; AIB-06; AQF-20; DIE-07; MAC-04; NTS-15; NTS-22; SEC-05; PPE-13

item_title: Fermentation and the Future of Europe's Protein System (Systemiq for The Protein Project)
scope_note: Food fermentation in scope; adoption volumes come from a market-substitution S-curve whose method is in an unpublished report, so they are not usable as findings
vietnam_angle: Its sugar-beet deep dive (crops and molasses as fermentation feedstock for farmers) is the EU analogue of T4 (cassava starch to fermentation sugar)
vietnam_evidence: T4 already rests on Vietnam's cassava starch exports to China (ch01 section 1.5; ch26)
verdict_note: Covered by T4 (feedstock), T5 (shared capacity), T7 and T9. The 2040 environmental figures assume 3% substitution of animal protein in the EU, a market projection the study's rules exclude
signal_to_watch: Publication of the Systemiq and GFI Europe adoption model with its method

item_title: Domestic-feed-only self-sufficiency stress test (method in PPE-03 and PPE-04)
scope_note: Measures the import exposure of the animal protein people eat
vietnam_angle: The study already attributes 61% to 71% of animal protein (2023) and 69% to 77% of meat protein to imports, directly or through feed; the EU test gives about 40% of EU livestock output lost without imported high-protein feed
vietnam_evidence: ch01 section 1.1 and wave 11 L4 tables
verdict_note: The study's attribution is the same idea on a wider base (it counts maize too). A formal domestic-feed-only rerun would not change any conclusion

item_title: Target-first back-calculation with feasibility grading of each lever (method in PPE-03 and PPE-04)
scope_note: Presentation method for the balance model
vietnam_angle: ch22 section 22.5 already grades the scenarios against real-world analogues (China, Norway, Japan); a lever-by-lever table would make the gap explicit
vietnam_evidence: Our run: the 20% EU-style target needs 1.74 Mt protein against trend; levers graded against Vietnamese benchmarks (2010 soybean area; D-BENCH and D-STRETCH; S-EFF and S-ALT) reach at most about 60% even when all are added, and the study has not tested them combined
verdict_note: Adds a feasibility-graded lever table to app-f4 and one sentence to ch22 section 22.5. Weakness to avoid: the EU version grades against literature ranges, not costs, and sets the target first

item_title: Legumes and pulses observatory: prices, volumes and demand (proposal in PPE-03 appendix and PPE-05)
vietnam_angle: Vietnam has no public series of domestic soybean or mung bean farm-gate prices (OQ-094 open since wave 1); P6 already plans a public price series for food protein ingredients
vietnam_evidence: Domestic soybean price known only from one 2024 press source (AQF-20); import unit values available from UN Comtrade (SEC-05)
verdict_note: Add domestic soybean and mung bean farm-gate prices and imported food-bean unit values by origin to the P6 price series

item_title: Closed-door multi-stakeholder forum as a way to prepare rules (method in PPE-06 and PPE-07)
vietnam_angle: The Food Safety Law window (first comments October 2026, vote considered May 2027) is the moment such a forum would matter
vietnam_evidence: We found no evidence that a non-state forum of NGOs and industry feeds Vietnamese food rule-making; drafting runs through MOH and public comment on the draft law (ch27)
verdict_note: The cheaper route in Vietnam is written comment on the draft law and decree (PO-015, PO-019). Our judgement, Low
signal_to_watch: A consumer association or industry body convening on the novel-food decree

item_title: Precedent: the 1973 US soybean export embargo and Japan's response (cited in PPE-03)
owner: University of Illinois, farmdoc daily (as read)
scope_note: Export restriction on the bean behind tofu and soy milk, and behind feed
maps_to: RM-21; shock_register.csv; app-f2 section F2.1.7; ch20
vietnam_angle: Vietnam's soybeans come 89% from Brazil and the United States (2025). The main supplier has embargoed soybean exports once (June to September 1973). Japan, then 97% import-dependent, answered by financing a new origin (Brazil) rather than home production
vietnam_evidence: Origins: Brazil 45.8%, United States 43.6% (2025, MAC-09); HHI 4,053 for soybeans (2023, SEC-05)
verdict_note: Add SHK-021 to the shock register and the precedent to RM-21 (monitor food-soybean origins; equal standards). No new move
signal_to_watch: Any US, Brazilian or Argentine export restriction on soybeans or meal
